verdict: FAIL G1/G2/G3 -> the recency qty-clamp STAYS. It is protective, worth about +$876 in August.
headline: Unclamping (trading the WANTED qty instead of the clamped qty) costs -$876 across 40 clamped August positions / 7 days. Helped 3 days, hurt 4, drop-best -$1,167. No kill-switch breach either way (G4 passes).
mechanism_as_measured: The clamp gives up modest upside on good days (+$291 forgone on 08-04, +$194 on 08-03) and buys large protection on bad days (-$921 saved on 08-07, -$521 on 08-10). Net protective. That is the correct shape for a variance control and it is earning its keep.

TWO_ERRORS_CAUGHT_IN_MY_OWN_ANALYSIS_BEF.error: LINEAR-SCALING ESTIMATE said unclamping EARNS +$1,254 (saved $3,839 on losers, cost $4,998 on winners).
TWO_ERRORS_CAUGHT_IN_MY_OWN_ANALYSIS_BEF.why_wrong: It computed counterfactual P&L as pnl_per_contract * wanted_qty. The prereg flagged this assumption as untrusted BEFORE running and required a real replay. Reported sign was wrong.
TWO_ERRORS_CAUGHT_IN_MY_OWN_ANALYSIS_BEF.detection: Prereg method clause mandating a non-linear replay.

TWO_ERRORS_CAUGHT_IN_MY_OWN_ANALYSIS_BEF.why_wrong: The wanted-qty lookup was keyed on (arm, symbol, date), but that key maps to MULTIPLE fills -- safe-3 split 2+1 lots on the same contract at 11:52 on 08-04, and several arms re-entered the same strike the same day. Every fill sharing a key got the full wanted qty, double-counting unclamped size.
TWO_ERRORS_CAUGHT_IN_MY_OWN_ANALYSIS_BEF.detection: Traced one position at qty 3 vs 8: per-contract P&L identical (+$81.8), proving the walker scales LINEARLY -- which contradicted the aggregate. The contradiction exposed the join bug.
TWO_ERRORS_CAUGHT_IN_MY_OWN_ANALYSIS_BEF.fix: Per-fill join: decision rows matched to fills by nearest timestamp within 300s, each decision row consumed at most once.

corrected_method: 40 clamped fleet positions, Aug 03-11. Each fill replayed TWICE through the real exit_manager via multileg_exit_walk at calibration v5 (extreme fills, $0.01 slippage, SPY union feed) -- at traded qty and at wanted qty -- entry time / premium / exit shape held fixed. 29 positions unmatched (core accounts safe-2/bold-2 have no fleet decision row; the clamp question is fleet-scoped).
REFINED_FINDING_FOR_NEXT_SESSION: The clamp is not the defect. Its per-arm RELEASE behaviour is the open question: risky-3 was NEVER clamped in August (FULL on every entry), and safe-3 flipped to FULL on exactly 2026-08-07 -- the two arms that took the biggest hits that day. risky-1, which stayed clamped through 08-07, was protected to the tune of $921. Question to prereg next: why is risky-3's recency state permanently GREEN, and should the clamp's release require more than a single good day?
rule6_check: At the WANTED qty, 0 of 41 clamped positions would breach the per-trade risk cap (safe 30% / bold-risky 50%). The clamp is a DISCRETIONARY reduction layered on top of Rule 6, not risk-rule enforcement.
